pairs.question: Alienae igitur culpae me reum subicies?
pairs.answer: Prorsus alienae, si provideri potuit ne exsisteret!
pairs.derivation: Brutus puts an objection in Cicero's mouth and answers it himself. The framing speech tag 'inquies' (interrupting the quoted question) is dropped as narration of the speaking; the question's own words are kept contiguous and in source order, first word capitalized. The answer 'prorsus alienae, si provideri potuit ne exsisteret' directly echoes and answers 'alienae... culpae'; it ends at the exclamation point, before the next sentence 'quod utinam inspectare possis timorem de illo meum!' which turns to a separate wish. First word capitalized.
